----- 1306 2026-11-21T04:17:54.121Z
Here are my resolutions of the two questions for you to approve or disapprove. The final critic is still reading the whole state, and nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**1. Do need-side environmental rows count as an identity's ICF rows?**
- **My resolution: no.** These rows record which needs serve an identity, with the ICF factors those needs work through. They don't count as the identity's own ICF coverage.
- **What changes if you approve:**
  - No rows change, and you can mark them stated as identity-to-need links.
  - Only BLIND (b210) and COM (b164) have an identity-side code today. The other 15 identities remain gaps under your 2026-11-20 rule that an identity with no ICF code is a gap to close.
  - I'd file a tooling gap that `lens-crosswalk --uncovered` should count only identity-side codes. As it stands, it would drop every identity once you review its rows.

**2. The `e120` and A-TRIGGER rows**
- **Keep (approve):**
  - Rows 53, 57 and 61 are `e120` (mobility products and technology) on LPA, TALL and BAR. A-SIZE's own ICF row holds it, and its obligation names seat width and weight rating, which are products.
  - Row 45 is EPI with `e240` (annotated flash/strobe). It matches the need's text on photosensitive epilepsy and flash thresholds.
  - Row 48 is COM with `e260` (air quality). It matches the need's text on MCAS and fragrance-free provision.
- **Reject (disapprove):**
  - Row 46 is EPI with `e260`.
  - Row 47 is COM with `e240`.
  - No record ties either pairing. They only exist because my rule attached every one of the need's codes to every identity. The first critic's pass 4 also flagged this split.
- **If you approve:** I append a ledger entry naming `TRIPLE-46` and `TRIPLE-47`, then reject those two rows through the review verb. A rejected row is retired and can't be edited. The other 65 rows stay pending.

Say "approve both", or name what you'd change.

**Also done:** I recorded "4 A-AT is in scope" in the ledger, closed GAP-380 on it, and paired A-AT with BLIND (2 rows, an inference, since the need names screen readers and magnification and no record names the identity). I did not pair A-AT with any other identity.
----- 1311 2026-11-21T04:18:01.493Z

1306 ASST 2026-11-21T04:17:54.121Z Here are my resolutions of the two questions for you to approve or disapprove. The final critic is still reading the whole state, and nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**1. Do need-side environmental rows count as an identity's ICF rows?**
- **My resolution: no.** These rows record which needs serve an identity, with the ICF factors those needs work through. They don't count as the identity's own ICF coverage.
- **What changes if you approve:**
  - No rows change, and you can mark them stated as identity-to-need links.
  - Only BLIND (b210) and COM (b164) have an identity-side code today. The other 15 identities remain gaps under your 2026-11-20 rule that an identity with no ICF code is a gap to close.
  - I'd file a tooling gap that `lens-crosswalk --uncovered` should count only identity-side codes. As it stands, it would drop every identity once you review its rows.

**2. The `e120` and A-TRIGGER rows**
- **Keep (approve):**
  - Rows 53, 57 and 61 are `e120` (mobility products and technology) on LPA, TALL and BAR. A-SIZE's own ICF row holds it, and its obligation names seat width and weight rating, which are products.
  - Row 45 is EPI with `e240` (annotated flash/strobe). It matches the need's text on photosensitive epilepsy and flash thresholds.
  - Row 48 is COM with `e260` (air quality). It matches the need's text on MCAS and fragrance-free provision.
- **Reject (disapprove):**
  - Row 46 is EPI with `e260`.
  - Row 47 is COM with `e240`.
  - No record ties either pairing. They only exist because my rule attached every one of the need's codes to every identity. The first critic's pass 4 also flagged this split.
- **If you approve:** I append a ledger entry naming `TRIPLE-46` and `TRIPLE-47`, then reject those two rows through the review verb. A rejected row is retired and can't be edited. The other 65 rows stay pending.

Say "approve both", or name what you'd change.

**Also done:** I recorded "4 A-AT is in scope" in the ledger, closed GAP-380 on it, and paired A-AT with BLIND (2 rows, an inference, since the need names screen readers and magnification and no record names the identity). I did not pair A-AT with any other identity.

1319 USER 2026-11-21T04:19:10.431Z 'what are need-side environmental rows?'
1321 ASST 2026-11-21T04:19:16.690Z A need-side environmental row is a row in the identity–need–ICF table whose ICF code starts with "e" and comes from the need's own list of codes, not from anything specific to the identity.

The ICF's "e" component covers environmental factors: the products, buildings, lighting and sound around a person. The project keeps a list per access need in `access_need_icf`. For example, A-NOSIGHT lists e125 (products and technology for communication), e150 (building design, public), e155 (building design, private) and e240 (light). Those titles are as recorded in `base_icf`.

For a pair I judged, such as BLIND with A-NOSIGHT, I wrote one row per code on the need's list:

| Identity | Need | ICF code |
|---|---|---|
| BLIND | A-NOSIGHT | e125 |
| BLIND | A-NOSIGHT | e150 |
| BLIND | A-NOSIGHT | e155 |
| BLIND | A-NOSIGHT | e240 |

The identity–need judgment is the real content: blind people are served by this need. The ICF codes are copied from the need's list, so every identity paired with A-NOSIGHT would get the same four rows. The "side" is the need's: the code describes what the need asks of the environment, not anything about blind people.

That is why I asked whether these rows count as the identity's ICF coverage. Almost every row in the table is this kind. Only two rows carry a code tied to the identity itself: BLIND with b210, and COM with b164.

None of the rows would change under either reading, and none has been reviewed yet. The difference is only how coverage is counted:
- **Yes:** an identity paired with a need that holds e150 or e240 counts as ICF-covered. I'd drop the proposed tooling gap.
- **No:** only identity-side codes count, as I proposed.

A "yes" also affects question 2, where I proposed rejecting two rows. Row 47 is COM with e240 (light). Light is a code you've just named as a concern, so I'd want to re-check it rather than reject it on my earlier reasoning.

**The subject moved while I read it.** A fifth ledger entry ("Owner statements 2026-11-21 (fifth)", `references/project-standards.md:8338`), migration `data_20261121042011_*` and the closing of GAP-378 landed mid-pass. The brief names four entries and GAP-378 as open. I reviewed the state as it stood at the end: 67 rows, 7 session migrations, 5 ledger entries, gaps 377/378/380 CLOSED-DECIDED, 379/381/382 OPEN.

Row ids are `triple_id` (identity|need|code).

## Findings, worst first

**F1. BLOCKER — GAP-378 is CLOSED-DECIDED on a "yes" the owner did not give.**
- **Artefacts:** ledger entry (fifth), lines 8338-8355; `data_20261121042011_*`; GAP-378 `resolution_ref` = `"our project is literally about artchitectural design techniques"`.
- **Clarifying question unanswered:** at 04:19:43.552 the coordinator asked whether question 1 "resolves to yes rather than my 'no'" (`main.jsonl` line 1339). The owner's next message was enqueued at 04:19:44.658 (line 1340), 1.1 s later. A 64-character message cannot be a typed reply to a question posted 1.1 s earlier; it continues the previous message. No later owner message answers it.
- **Entry stronger than the words:** the entry admits "the owner did not write 'yes'" and brackets the reading as an ASSUMPTION. ACTION (1) then states it as an imperative: "Count a need-side environmental row as the identity's ICF coverage; do not file or build a change that excludes it".
- **Reversal:** the coordinator had recommended "no" twice (lines 1195, 1306), and the 2026-11-20 entry's ACTION (3) reads an identity with no ICF code as a gap to close.
- **Consequence:** once the rows are reviewed, every paired identity leaves `lens-crosswalk --uncovered` on an inferred answer.
- **Header:** it says both messages came after the coordinator "asked whether such rows count". Only the explanation at 04:19:16 precedes the first message; the direct question precedes the second by 1.1 s.
- **False if:** an owner message after 04:19:43 says yes to the question as put.

**F2. MUST-AMEND — row 64 (BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|b210): three legs with no record under them.**
- **Code not named by the owner:** the owner typed "1 yes b is seeing therefore ties into blind etc" (line 1214). "b210" is not in the words.
- **Where b210 = seeing came from:** the coordinator's own explanation at 02:19:46 (line 1180), "b210 seeing functions", which it flags as "from my general knowledge of the ICF, not from the project". `base_icf.title` for b210 is NULL. No WHO payload was fetched. This is "titles from memory" recurring one step removed.
- **Only project record of b210 is the retired axis layer:** `base_icf.notes` = "seeded from axes.icf_b_anchors", and `governance/functional-taxonomy.md:158-159` (AX-VIS-L, AX-VIS-N). The third entry itself says a body-function row "still needs a basis that is not an axis anchor".
- **Ledger restates the assumption as fact:** ACTION (2) of the third entry, outside the ASSUMPTION bracket: "The only body-function tie the owner's words state is b210 to the blind identity".
- **Need leg unsupported and undisclosed:** `access_need_icf` holds no A-NOSIGHT -> b210 row. It is the only row of 67 whose code is not in its need's map. The owner tied b to blind, not to a need; the warrant does not say the need key was the author's choice.
- **Review surface:** `v_lens_crosswalk.icf_title` renders NULL for this row, so the owner approves a code whose meaning the row cannot show.
- **Pass record:** finding 193 (L7-recognition, HIGH) names "BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|b210" as the sharpest case and is disposed REPAIRED. The row is back.
- **False if:** a fetched WHO payload for b210 is logged, and an owner statement names b210 and its need.

**F3. MUST-AMEND — row 65 (COM|A-TIME|b164): false quotation attribution recurs; finding 191's REPAIRED is no longer true.**
- **Warrant:** `Need A-TIME registry text read: "brain fog impairs organizing time"`.
- **Evidence:** the string is in no column of `access_needs` for A-TIME (absorbs = "slow processing, motor delay, AAC use, screen-reader navigation, translation, distraction"). It is in `access_need_icf.notes` for (A-TIME, b164). In the other 66 rows "registry text" resolves to `access_needs.absorbs`.
- **Self-contradiction:** the warrant's later sentence names the true home, so the row contradicts itself.
- **Pass record:** this is finding 191 exactly ("this one is in access_need_icf.notes, not access_needs.absorbs"). It was REPAIRED at 02:10 by withholding the row, then the row was written at 02:24 with the same mislabel.
- **Cause:** `build_triples.py:97-99` accepts a need quote from absorbs, notes or ICF notes and labels all three "registry text".
- **Against the session's own ledger:** third entry ACTION (2) requires "its own recorded basis" for every identity and code other than b210 and BLIND. The warrant says of the identity leg "No record read stated this link". It puts a cognitive-function impairment code on people with ME/CFS and long COVID by inference.
- **Repair cost:** the warrant is immutable (trigger `identity_need_icf_no_edit`); correction needs an owner-referenced retirement.

**F4. MUST-AMEND — gap text now false or misleading.** All derive commands run; results below.
- **GAP-377 (closed):**
  - "The matrix therefore proposes no b-code row" is false: `select substr(icf_code,1,1),count(*) …` gives b 2, e 65.
  - "Body-function rows that would have rested on the retired axis layer were not proposed and are not offered": `withheld.json` prints only `COM A-TIME b164`. BLIND|b210 was therefore in the not-offered class and is now a row.
- **GAP-378 (closed):**
  - "Every row … is a judged identity-need pair crossed with the codes the need's own access_need_icf rows hold" is false for row 64. The same sentence is the `disposition_ref` of finding 197.
  - "Derive the identities that hold a row with an activity code: … `<>'e'` (empty at filing)" now returns BLIND and COM, which hold body-function codes. The query's label is wrong.
- **GAP-380 (closed):**
  - "No identity-need-ICF triple was proposed for it" is false (rows 66, 67).
  - The derive returns A-PRECISION, A-REACH, A-SELFCARE; the "At filing" list for A-TIME is historical.
- **GAP-379 (open):** the "keyed on the whole identity" query presents itself as the umbrella rows. It now also returns BLIND|A-AT (2) and returns EPI|A-TRIGGER (2); neither is an umbrella. The hand rows 66/67 reuse the umbrella phrase for a different meaning.
- **GAP-382 (open):** "attacked by four read-only passes" and "The final version of the rows had no pass of its own" are stale. `grep -rl identity_need_icf scripts/audit` still prints nothing (rc 1), so that part holds.
- **GAP-381 (open):** (1) returns MOB, SCI, ALL, LMB, MOVE, VES as stated. (2) holds: 43 of 72 `base_icf` titles NULL. (3) `lens-crosswalk --uncovered` was not run.

**F5. MUST-AMEND — pass 10 covers none of the final rows.**
- `subject_commit` 141b42d is the 135-row first version. Finding subject keys cite d-codes and "all 135", none of which exist now.
- No recorded pass has the 67 rows as its subject. GAP-382 discloses this for the 63; it predates rows 64-67.
- REPAIRED on 191 and 193 is contradicted by rows 65 and 64 (F2, F3).

**F6. NOTE — hand rows bypass the generator's own tense guard.**
- `build_triples.py:80` refuses " is ", " are " and others outside quotations.
- Row 64: "said that b is seeing and ties into blind".
- Rows 66, 67: "that these are the technologies this identity uses".
- Rows 13, 14 (generator-built): "that aphasia follows stroke" ("follows" is not in the guard list).
- All are reported-content clauses; review does not falsify them. The "past tense" claim is literally untrue for 5 rows.

**F7. NOTE — ledger quoting.**
- Fourth entry quotes "4 A-AT is in scope" and silently drops the rest of the message, "alsdo double check your wqork" (line 1274). No elision is marked.
- A first `close-gap GAP-380` was refused because the quote occurred twice (`refusals.jsonl`). The entry's derive command was then reworded by `sed` (line 1286) so it occurs once.
- Second entry lists COM, BRAIN and MH as umbrellas "beside the rows keyed on its members". The registry holds no member identities for those three; only NDV has AUT and ADHD.
- First entry's supersession line (ACTION (2) of the fifth 2026-11-20 entry) sits outside any ASSUMPTION bracket, though the owner's words begin "I think".

**F8. NOTE — migration summary names content the file lacks.** `data_20261121041650_*` summary says "and the closing of the gap that asked"; the file holds 2 `identity_need_icf` INSERTs only. The closing is in `041701`.

**F9. NOTE — other things a reviewer would be misled by.**
- Rows 42-44 (MH|A-STIMULUS): the template says the need "named a condition that the identity's description listed". PTSD is not listed; the warrant adds "was read as falling under" trauma. It is an inference not caught by the `'%recorded as an inference%'` query.
- Rows 8-10 (DEAFBLIND|A-TACTILE): the identity quotation is "Not VIS+DEAF". It is a true substring of the description but does not show the covering the template asserts.
- Selective inference: BLIND|A-AT was proposed on "screen readers, magnification". A-TIME's absorbs holds "screen-reader navigation", and no BLIND|A-TIME row was proposed.
- Double counting: BLIND holds e125 under A-NOSIGHT (row 1) and A-AT (row 66). Nine (identity, code) combinations repeat across needs; `select identity_code,icf_code,count(*) … having count(*)>1` lists them.
- Rows 46 (EPI|e260) and 47 (COM|e240) are still pending. The coordinator has told the owner no record ties either.

- **Rows (67):**
  - All `pending`, unreviewed, unretired, one session stamp.
  - No MOB, LMB, SCI, MOVE, VES or ALL row.
  - No axis word or `AX-` code outside quotations.
  - 31 pairs. All 62 need and identity quotations are substrings of a live cell; 61 are in the cell the warrant names (exception F3).
  - 66 of 67 codes are in the need's `access_need_icf` set, and each pair carries the need's full set (exception row 64).
  - The five NDV warrants' "ledger, third set" resolves to line 6019, "retain MH and NDV and TALL".
- **Ledger:** all seven quoted owner strings are in `transcripts/harness_de695d5a/main.jsonl` verbatim (trailing spaces trimmed). The three `resolution_ref` quotes each occur once. Entries 1, 2 and 4 keep their readings in ASSUMPTION brackets.
- **Migrations (7):**
  - The rebuild succeeds at `user_version` 166.
  - 64 tables compared; only `data_migrations` differs. `foreign_key_check` is empty.
  - Statement census: 67 triple, 14 finding, 1 pass and 6 gap INSERTs; 10 finding, 1 pass and 4 gap UPDATEs. No other table is touched.
- **Pass 10:** 14 findings match the first critic's closing block on all eight fields, with 12 lenses present.
